user.title: Connect to a SPIFFE Workload API
user.description: Home Assistant gets its SPIFFE identity from a Workload API served on a Unix socket, for example by an agent running as an app (add-on). Any SPIFFE implementation works.

data_description.socket: A unix:// address as Home Assistant sees it, such as unix:///config/.spiffe/agent.sock
A unix:// address as Home Assistant sees it, such as unix:///config/.spiffe/agent.sock

error.invalid_socket: This is not a valid address. Use unix:///absolute/path/to/agent.sock.
error.socket_missing: There is no socket at this path yet. Start the agent first, then try again.
error.cannot_connect: The socket exists but the Workload API did not answer. Check that the agent is running and can reach its issuer.

abort.reconfigure_successful: The Workload API address was changed.

workload_api_unreachable.title: The SPIFFE Workload API is not answering
workload_api_unreachable.description:
For more than five minutes, Home Assistant could not reach the Workload API at {socket}. Integrations that use SPIFFE cannot get tokens until it answers again.

Check that the agent is running. The last error was: {error}

permission_denied.title: No SPIFFE identity has been issued to Home Assistant
permission_denied.description:
The Workload API answers, but refused to issue a JWT-SVID. Usually this means Home Assistant has not been admitted (registered) at the issuer yet, or the audience requested is not allowed.

The error was: {error}
